prompt: This page is cited in drug-encyclopedia entries on synthetic cathinones, for these substances: 4-BMC (brephedrone). Report from the page, exactly as printed (numbers digit by digit, names in the page's own spelling and punctuation, lists complete and in page order): (1) chemical identifiers and names for each of these substances: every name used (INN, systematic, IUPAC or chemical name, other names, synonyms, abbreviations and code names), CAS number(s), molecular formula, molecular weight or molar mass, ATC code, and schedule or control status; (2) forms and products: physical forms, appearance, formulations, product types, product or brand names, packaging, and any seizure or drug-checking findings described (briefly, keeping key terms in the page's wording). Say 'not given' for anything the page does not contain. Do not add anything that is not on the page, and do not quote any passage longer than 15 words.
answer:
**(1) Identifiers, names and control status**

- **Common names:** 4-BMC; 4-Bromomethcathinone; Brephedrone; 4-BMAP; p-BMC; para-BMC; p-Bromomethcathinone; para-Bromomethcathinone; 4-Bromo-methcathinone; 4-Br-methcathinone; 4-Bromo-N-methylcathinone; 4-Br-MCAT; 4-Bromo MC
- **EUDA framework name:** 4Br-MC
- **Systematic (IUPAC) name:** 1-(4-Bromophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one; (RS)-1-(4-bromophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one
- **Other chemical names:** 1-(4-Bromophenyl)-2-(methylamino)-1-propanone; 4′-Bromo-2-(methylamino)propanophenone; 2-(Methylaminol-l-(4-bromophenyl)propan-l-one (as printed)
- **CAS numbers:** 486459-03-4 (base); 135333-27-6 (hydrochloride salt); 1388142-13-9 (R-isomer); 1388142-14-0 (S-isomer)
- **Molecular formula:** C10H12BrNO
- **Molecular mass:** 242.11 (as printed, no unit given)
- **ATC code:** not given
- **InChI Keys and SMILES:** provided for the base, hydrochloride salt, and R/S isomers (see page 18-19)
- **Control status:**
  - Restricted in 20 Member States, Türkiye and Norway, sometimes under a generic cathinone definition.
  - Not restricted in seven Member States (Bulgaria, Greece, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Romania, Slovakia, Spain). The Netherlands plans coverage by a generic definition from 1 July 2025.
  - Controlled in China since October 2015.
  - Not controlled in India, per available information.
  - Not under assessment, and not previously assessed, by the UN system (WHO, 20 March 2025).
  - Schedule status under UN conventions: not given for 4-BMC itself. The page lists the parent cathinone and methcathinone as Schedule I, and 4-MMC as Schedule II.

**(2) Forms, products and findings**

- **Physical form:** Hydrochloride salt described as a solid. Seizures and samples were mostly powder, with some tablets and capsules. The page reports one powder described as white and three described as yellow (2025 cases).
- **Appearance and properties:** Solubility in DMF, DMSO, ethanol and PBS (pH 7.2) is listed. λmax is 264 nm. Melting points are 97.6 °C (SWGDRUG) and 186–189 °C (Foley and Cozzi).
- **Formulations and brand/product names:** not given.
- **Packaging:** not given.
- **Seizures:** 754 seizures and imports (2011–2024), 739 of them powder. About 1,069.7 kg of powder, of which roughly 1,038 kg was a 2024 import from India. Most cases (630) contained 4-BMC alone.
- **Drug checking:** 11 samples from 2024, all powders. In nine, 4-BMC was the only substance. Two contained other substances: 2-MMC, NEP and 2-CMC in one, and MDMA in another. In eight cases it was mis-sold as 3-MMC; in two, as 4-MMC.
- **Other reported forms:** Six cases of tablets and capsules, and nine cases of other or unknown form.
